title: observability: propagate request_id and trace context through streaming & OpenAI compat layer; add per-endpoint metrics tags and structured logs
author: Ava Chen
body: Motivation: We need consistent request tracing and observability across the API surface including streaming endpoints, the OpenAI compatibility proxy, function/tool-calling responses, and structured output paths. This change ensures a single request_id is assigned at the gateway and propagated through all downstream services and streaming frames; it also propagates W3C traceparent/tracecontext where present, and tags per-endpoint metrics with route and model metadata so dashboards and alerts can be accurate. Summary of changes: 1) Gateway: generate/accept request_id header (X-Request-Id) and prefer incoming header if present; attach traceparent header to outgoing internal requests when available. 2) Streaming runtime: include request_id and trace context in each stream frame metadata (kept compact to avoid payload bloat), and ensure SSE/HTTP2 streaming compat with OpenAI-style event frames. 3) OpenAI compatibility layer: map inbound OpenAI-style request_id/trace headers into our internal headers and mirror them back on responses; support function/tool-call events with structured JSON envelopes and request_id/trace fields. 4) Structured logs: add request_id and trace id as top-level fields in all API access logs and structured runtime logs; update log schema version to 2. 5) Metrics: add endpoint_tags to api.request.* metrics and runtime tokenization/latency metrics; tags include route, model_family, model_variant, customer_tier. 6) Tests & docs: unit/integration tests for header propagation, streaming frames, and backward compatibility; updated docs in redwood-docs quickstart and OpenAI-compat guide. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is no-op for clients that do not send request_id/traceparent; the gateway will create a request_id so downstream users get correlation even for legacy clients. Rollout: feature flagged by obs.request_propagation; deploy to staging for 48h then gradual canary across regions. CI: initial CI flake resolved (streaming integration), final CI green. See commits for granular changes and reviewer thread below.
commits: 4d1f3a2: gateway: add request_id extraction/generation and traceparent forwarding
b7c9e10: streaming: attach compact frame metadata for request_id/trace and ensure SSE compatibility
c8a4b2f: openai-compat: map incoming x-request-id/traceparent into internal headers and mirror back
9f2d3ac: logs: bump structured log schema to v2 and include request_id/trace_id fields
e5a77b1: metrics: add endpoint tags to api.request.* and runtime.* metrics
0a3b4d6: tests: add integration tests for propagation and streaming frames
review_comments: Ravi Patel: Please ensure we do not leak PII in the streaming frame metadata; prefer hashed ids for customer-visible IDs.
Ava Chen: Agreed, we only include our internal request_id and traceparent; customer ids are present only when explicitly provided and are hashed in logs per policy.
Diego Martinez: Two nits: 1) header name normalization in compat layer; 2) metrics cardinality check — have you validated tag cardinality for model_variant?
Ava Chen: Fixed header canonicalization and added limits on unique model_variant tags with a safe fallback 'unknown_variant' to prevent explosion.
Priya Nair: Integration test flaked once on the CI runner (timeout) — did you increase the stream timeout?
Ava Chen: Increased stream timeout and added retry in test harness; CI passed on re-run and logs confirm stable passing.
Ravi Patel: Approving after minor comments addressed.
release_notes: Added request_id/trace propagation across gateway, streaming runtime, and OpenAI compatibility layer; structured logs now include request_id and trace_id; API metrics include per-endpoint tags. Rollout behind feature flag obs.request_propagation.
